name: West India Cocoa-Nut Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: sixteen eggs (omitting the whites of four)
ingredients.originalText: sixteen eggs (omitting the whites of four)

instructions.text: Cut up and skin a large ripe cocoa-nut and grate it fine
Put the grated cocoa-nut into a clean cloth and squeeze and press it till all the moisture is taken out
Spread it on a broad tin pan and stand it up to dry, either in the sun or before the fire, stirring it up occasionally with your hands
When quite dry weigh a pound of it
Beat very light sixteen eggs omitting the whites of four and then beat into them, gradually, a pound of powdered loaf-sugar and a wine glass of rose-water
Give the whole a hard stirring
Put the mixture into deep dishes and lay puff-paste round their edges handsomely notched
Bake them about half an hour
Send them to table cold with white sugar grated over the top

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cut up and skin a large ripe cocoa-nut and grate it fine
2. Put the grated cocoa-nut into a clean cloth and squeeze and press it till all the moisture is taken out
3. Spread it on a broad tin pan and stand it up to dry, either in the sun or before the fire, stirring it up occasionally with your hands
4. When quite dry weigh a pound of it
5. Beat very light sixteen eggs omitting the whites of four and then beat into them, gradually, a pound of powdered loaf-sugar and a wine glass of rose-water
6. Give the whole a hard stirring
7. Put the mixture into deep dishes and lay puff-paste round their edges handsomely notched
8. Bake them about half an hour
9. Send them to table cold with white sugar grated over the top
